government_link: Yes — Mubadala Investment Company (Abu Dhabi sovereign investor) is the anchor shareholder (stake not verified in this batch); designated a Domestic Systemically Important Bank by CBUAE with a D-SIB buffer from 30 Jun 2026 (S4).

name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank
legal_name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank Public Joint Stock Company
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX with 3,632,000,000 shares. At 31 Dec 2025 the only holders above 5% were Emirates International Investment Company LLC (1,431,110,701 shares, 39.40%) and Emirates NBD PJSC (246,223,389 shares, 6.78%); other investors held 53.82%. UAE nationals held 73.3% and foreign investors 26.7% (foreign cap 40%). In Sep 2026 the board proposed an AED 1.75bn rights issue (up to 106.383m new shares at AED 16.45); the investor presentation says major shareholders confirmed full-entitlement participation.
government_link: Not established from opened sources for equity: the ultimate owner of the 39.40% holder (Emirates International Investment Company) was not verified. The Abu Dhabi Government (Department of Finance) holds AED 2bn of Tier 1 sukuk issued on 16 Apr 2009 under the Abu Dhabi bank capitalisation programme. That is capital, not ordinary equity (FY2025 FS).

name: Ajman Bank
ownership_summary: Listed on DFM. At 31 Dec 2025 the Government of Ajman held 33.10% and H.H. Sheikh Humaid bin Rashid Al Nuaimi (Ruler of Ajman) 15.98%; free float was 50.92%. The FY2025 earnings review describes 58% ownership by the Emirate of Ajman and the ruling family 'directly and indirectly'. No merger, recapitalisation or change of control found for 2024–2026. Capital actions were debt-based: a senior sukuk in 2025 and an inaugural USD 300m AT1 sukuk in Jul 2026.
government_link: Yes — the Government of Ajman holds 33.1% and the interim statements say the Group 'is controlled by Ajman Government' (30 Jun 2026). The Ruler of Ajman holds a further 15.98%, and the Crown Prince of Ajman chairs the board.

name: Al Masraf (Arab Bank for Investment and Foreign Trade)
legal_name: Arab Bank for Investment and Foreign Trade PJSC
ownership_summary: Unlisted PJSC with three shareholders. The Emirates Investment Authority (EIA), the UAE federal government's sovereign wealth fund, holds 60.00%, Libyan Foreign Bank 29.30% and Banque Extérieure d'Algérie 10.70% (30 Jun 2026). EIA became majority owner on 6 Nov 2025 by buying 12.98% from Libyan Foreign Bank and 4.74% from Banque Extérieure d'Algérie (CBUAE-approved). Before that the split was 42.28% / 42.28% / 15.44% (31 Dec 2024).
government_link: Yes: majority-owned (60%) by the Emirates Investment Authority, the only sovereign wealth fund of the UAE Federal Government (since 6 Nov 2025). The other 40% is held by Libyan and Algerian state banks. The bank calls itself 'the UAE's Federal Commercial Bank' (S4, S1, S9).

name: Al Ramz Capital
legal_name: Al Ramz Corporation Investment and Development P.J.S.C.

government_link: Unclear. The company names the 'Abu Dhabi Wealth Fund' as its largest shareholder since 2009, without saying who owns it or its current stake.

legal_name: Arqaam Capital Limited (DIFC operating entity); group parent is Arqaam Capital Limited (Cayman Islands)

Newer investors, stakes undisclosed: Ethmar International Holding of Abu Dhabi (May 2025) and Bader Nasser Al-Kharafi / BNK Group with National Investments Company (NIC) of Kuwait (7 Jul 2026). Checked 12 Oct 2026; no wind-down or sale of the firm found.
government_link: Indirect and minority only: Wafra (PIFSS Kuwait, a government social-security institution), Emirates NBD (largely Dubai Government owned) and CBI (largely Qatar and Ras Al Khaimah government linked) are named 5%+ holders per the firm's page (S4). No controlling state shareholder. Checked 2026-10-12.
aum_period: As stated in the firm's statement of 13 May 2025

name: Baraka
legal_name: Baraka Financial Limited (DIFC company no. 4153); ultimate holding company Baraka Technology Holding Ltd (ADGM company no. 4143)
ownership_summary: Privately held, venture-backed. No later priced round found as of 12 Oct 2026. Shareholding percentages are not disclosed.
government_link: None found. No government or sovereign investor among disclosed backers (checked 2026-10-12).

name: Bank of Sharjah
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX; the Government of Sharjah, through Sharjah Asset Management, is the largest shareholder with 39.25% at 31 Dec 2025, after an AED 800m capital increase approved on 4 May 2023 lifted its stake from 17.16% to about 40% and share capital to AED 3bn. United Alsaqer Group (linked to Deputy Chairman Sheikh Saif bin Mohammed bin Butti Al Hamed) holds 9.31%. No ownership change, merger or recapitalisation found for 2024–2026 (checked 2026-10-12).
government_link: Yes — Government of Sharjah via Sharjah Asset Management (39.25% at 31 Dec 2025). The Ruler of Sharjah is Honorary Chairman, the Chairman chairs the Sharjah Finance Department, and the CEO of Sharjah Asset Management sits on the board (board page checked 2026-10-12).

name: Commercial Bank of Dubai
ownership_summary: DFM-listed. At 31 Dec 2025 the Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD) held 20% on behalf of the Government of Dubai; four other holders above 5% held 40.35%: Al Futtaim Private Co. LLC 17.46%, Orient Insurance PJSC 8.84%, Abdul Wahed Al Rostamani (AWR) Group 7.68% and Ghobash Trading & Investment Co. 6.37%; UAE nationals held 99.81% (AT1 prospectus 13 Jul 2026, S5; annual report 2025, S6; shareholder list updated Mar 2026, S10). Foreign ownership allowed up to 40% since Jun 2020.
government_link: Yes — 20% held by the Investment Corporation of Dubai on behalf of the Government of Dubai (as of 31 Dec 2025, S5). The prospectus states neither the Government nor ICD has a legal obligation to fund CBD. The Chairman and one other director were elected as ICD representatives (S6).

name: Commercial Bank International
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX. Qatar National Bank (QNB) is the largest shareholder with 40% and has four non-independent board seats, including the Vice Chairman. The Bin Owaida family and business hold 22.40% and Mohd Omar Bin Haidar Investment 8.87% (all at 31 Dec 2025). The annual report says the majority of shareholders are UAE citizens and include the Government of Ras Al Khaimah (stake not disclosed). Share capital was unchanged at AED 1,737m from 31 Dec 2024 to 30 Jun 2026, although a rights issue of up to AED 889.1m was approved in Jul 2023. No merger or change of control found for 2024–2026 (official sources checked 2026-10-12).
government_link: Limited. The annual report says shareholders include the Government of Ras Al Khaimah (below the 5% disclosure threshold) and the bank was set up by Emiri Decree of the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah. The largest shareholder is Qatar National Bank (40%).

name: Dubai Islamic Bank
ownership_summary: Listed on DFM. The only shareholder above 5% is Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD), with 2,024,955,636 shares or 27.97% at 31 Dec 2025 (shareholder table; the related-party note rounds it to 27.9%). ICD is majority-owned by the Government of Dubai.
government_link: Yes. Investment Corporation of Dubai (majority-owned by the Government of Dubai) holds 27.97% (31 Dec 2025). The former chairman (to 20 Sep 2026) was Director-General of the Dubai Ruler's Court and Managing Director of ICD.

name: Emirates Islamic
ownership_summary: Wholly owned subsidiary of Emirates NBD Bank (P.J.S.C.). ENBD held ~99.9% until 2025, then acquired the remaining minority; EI shares were suspended on DFM from 10 Jun 2025 and the bank was delisted, becoming 100% owned. Ultimate parent is Investment Corporation of Dubai, wholly owned by the Government of Dubai (EI H1 2026 financial statements, note 1).
government_link: Yes - indirectly: 100% owned by Emirates NBD, whose ultimate parent is Investment Corporation of Dubai, wholly owned by the Government of Dubai (as of 30 Jun 2026).

name: Emirates Investment Bank
ownership_summary: Subsidiary of Al Futtaim Private Company LLC, which holds 92.39% (30 Jun 2026 and 31 Dec 2025). The 7.61% free float is held by individuals, and the shares have been listed on DFM since 2005 with very limited trading in 2025. One director holds an indirect 15% interest through Al Futtaim Private Co. LLC (governance report 2025).
government_link: No. Privately controlled by the Al Futtaim family group (Al Futtaim Private Company LLC, 92.39%) (S1, S3).

name: Emirates NBD
ownership_summary: DFM-listed. The H1 2026 financial statements name Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD), wholly owned by the Government of Dubai, as the Group's parent. Holders above 5% (ownership statistics as at 14 Jul 2026): ICD 40.9%, DH 7 LLC 14.8%, Capital Assets LLC 5.3%; free float 38.8%; foreign ownership 14.4% against a 40% limit. ENBD's 2 Aug 2026 DFM release describes it as 56% owned by the Dubai Government via ICD and Dubai Holding Group.
government_link: Yes - parent is Investment Corporation of Dubai, wholly owned by the Government of Dubai (H1 2026 financial statements, note 1); ENBD states it is 56% owned by the Dubai Government via ICD and Dubai Holding Group (DFM release, 2 Aug 2026).

name: First Abu Dhabi Bank

The Chairman is H.H. Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi.
government_link: Yes. Mubadala Investment Company (Abu Dhabi sovereign investor) holds 37.9% and the Abu Dhabi Ruling Family 17.7% (30 Jun 2026); Chairman is the Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi (board page checked 2026-10-12).

government_link: Indirect: ultimate parent International Holding Company PJSC is an ADX-listed Abu Dhabi conglomerate. IHC's own shareholder base was not assessed in this profile.

name: Invest Bank
ownership_summary: Government-controlled after two rescues. The Government of Sharjah took 50.07% in 2019 (1,592,857,143 new shares at AED 0.7, approved by the AGM on 10 Apr 2019) and then recapitalised the bank under a plan approved by the EGM on 27 Apr 2023. That plan comprised an AED 2.6bn rights issue, which took share capital to AED 3.2bn in about 263bn shares of AED 0.0121684 nominal, plus a Government of Sharjah guarantee over legacy assets (originally AED 3.0bn, reduced to AED 1.26bn in H1 2026). Capital Intelligence (Oct 2026) says the Government of Sharjah owns 88% directly and indirectly; Argaam (Oct 2025) gives about 70% Government of Sharjah and 18% Sharjah Social Security Fund. An EGM on 15 Oct 2026 votes on a 1-for-82.18 share consolidation back to AED 1 nominal, with capital unchanged at AED 3.2bn.
government_link: Yes — the Government of Sharjah owns 88% directly and indirectly (Capital Intelligence, 7 Oct 2026). It is the 'ultimate controlling party' and gives a special guarantee covering legacy-asset losses (AED 1.26bn remaining in H1 2026).

Co. 32.0%, Masar Investments 12.7% and other shareholders 12.8%, and states that the Al Ghurair family has held a majority stake since founding in 1967. The two Al Ghurair-named holders total 74.4%; the presentation does not say whether Masar Investments is a family entity.
government_link: No government shareholder shown in the June 2026 shareholding chart (S5). Designated a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB) by the CBUAE during 2025 (S4).

(7.317%), out of 3,659.0m shares and 10,004 shareholders; 69.26% of shares were held by UAE investors. name: Wio Bank
ownership_summary: Unlisted PJSC with AED 2.3bn paid-in capital, owned at 31 Dec 2025 by Alpha Dhabi Holding (33.15%), ADQ / Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company (31.85%), Etisalat (e&, 25%) and First Abu Dhabi Bank (10%). On 30 Jan 2026 Abu Dhabi's Supreme Council for Financial and Economic Affairs consolidated ADQ's assets and investments under L'IMAD Holding, naming Wio Bank among the portfolio companies; no Wio disclosure of a change in the registered 31.85% holder was found (checked 12 Oct 2026).

name: Zand Bank

Zand's Aug 2026 release says it is backed by 'an Abu Dhabi ruling family-owned investment arm', Franklin Templeton, Aditya Birla Group (via Solfrid Investments), Mohamed Alabbar and Yusuff Ali; the 2022 board release names Al Hail Holding LLC and Global Development Group as represented shareholders. Existing shareholders injected a further AED 250m in Sep 2025, and the merger with related entity Eradah Capital LLC (completed 26 Dec 2025) raised paid-up capital to AED 2.35bn.
government_link: Indirect / unclear: Zand describes one backer as 'an Abu Dhabi ruling family-owned investment arm' (Aug 2026) but does not name it or its stake. No federal or emirate government shareholder disclosed. Checked 2026-10-12.

name: Bahrain Islamic Bank

NBB first took control in 2020 (78.8% after its offer) and fully consolidates BisB. The only other holder above 5% is the Kuwait Awqaf Public Foundation (7.18% at 31 Dec 2025). Bahraini holders own 87.65% by nationality (31 Dec 2025).
government_link: Indirect - controlled by NBB (80.2%), in which Bahrain Mumtalakat Holding Company holds 44.06% (see bh-nbb); the Kuwait Awqaf Public Foundation (7.18%) is described in the AR as a sovereign holder.

government_link: Yes - 97.226% held by PIF (Saudi sovereign wealth fund); remaining shares held by KIA, Qatar Holding, Mumtalakat, OIA and UAE Ministry of Finance (S3, checked 2026-10-12).

ownership_summary: Listed on Boursa Kuwait since 15 May 2006. National Bank of Kuwait is the parent and the only holder above 5%, with 60.368% at 31 Dec 2025 (Boubyan AR 2025); NBK reports 60.4% (NBK AR 2025; 2Q 2026 presentation). A Boubyan-Gulf Bank merger study was called off on 14 Jan 2025.
government_link: No direct government holding above 5% disclosed; controlled by NBK (60.4%), which has no controlling shareholder.

The FY2025 annual report shows KIPCO (effective) 61%, PIFSS 8% and others 31%. A KD 50m rights issue (277.8m shares at 180 fils) closed on 14 Sep 2026, 133.57% subscribed, raising paid-up capital from KD 399.6m to KD 427.4m; KIPCO publicly committed to it on 12 Sep 2026, but its post-issue stake was not found.
government_link: Indirect - PIFSS (Kuwaiti state pension institution) held 8% per the FY2025 annual report; the controlling shareholder KIPCO is a listed private-sector holding company.

Warba completed its purchase of Al Ghanem Trading in April 2025, and the two banks signed an MoU in 2025 to assess a merger into one Sharia-compliant bank. The assessment is ongoing: due diligence 'nearing completion' (24 May 2026) and moving 'in an orderly manner' (3 Aug 2026); no definitive agreement found as of 12 Oct 2026. Gulf Bank is separately converting to a Sharia-compliant bank (CBK initial approval Aug 2025).
government_link: Partial - the Public Institution for Social Security (a Kuwaiti public institution) holds 7.19% at 31 Dec 2025; no controlling government holding.

government_link: No direct government shareholder identified; the controlling group (KIPCO / Burgan Bank / UGB) is privately controlled and listed.
